description:
Two related blind-spots flagged that TODOs whose safety predicate rests
on external/transient evidence (upstream behavior, harness output,
dependency-resolved version) have no schema-level mechanism to record
or verify the evidence durability:

- `2026-05-04-074634` -- the /todo review rubric scores write-time
  quality, not implement-time freshness. A TODO that sits in planning/
  for weeks may have evidence that has silently rotted.
- `2026-05-04-083819` -- W0 verification-only commits cite evidence in
  free-text commit messages; a reviewer landing the PR days later
  cannot replay it.

This TODO ships three thin conventions:

1. Optional `freshness_check` block in the TODO schema, OR a strong-
   convention "w0: re-validate evidence" first work unit for upstream-
   dependent items (w1 picks).
2. A new freshness axis on the /todo review rubric -- unconditionally,
   regardless of which mechanism w1 picks. The rubric must score
   freshness whether the schema field exists or the convention is
   review-time-only.
3. A `_project/verification-logs/<todo-id>/<work-id>.log` committed-
   artifact convention for verification-only commits.

The companion `extend-five-axis-review-rubric` TODO ships the
/code review side (verification-only / evidence-durability branch);
this TODO owns the /todo review side and the artifact convention.

anti_patterns.dont: capture verification logs that contain secrets or local-machine paths
anti_patterns.why: the convention is for upstream-evidence transcripts (e.g. `pip show sqlglot`, harness stdout), not for runtime traces.
backwards-incompatible schema changes break every existing TODO file.

anti_patterns.dont: skip the rubric update in w3 even if w1 picks the schema path
anti_patterns.why: the rubric is the durable enforcement layer regardless of mechanism.

preserves.behavior: /todo review rubric existing axes (clarity / completeness / actionability / freshness / guardrails / work-breakdown) are unchanged in name and weight.
Existing TODO files validate against the unchanged schema (the new field is optional).

verifications.description: validate_todo accepts an example TODO using the new field/convention
/todo review rubric carries a freshness axis

work_units.notes:
Choose between (a) adding `freshness_check:` as a new optional
field in `_project/TODO_ENTRY_TEMPLATE.yaml` + `validate_todo.py`,
or (b) elevating "w0: re-validate research evidence" to a strong
naming convention enforced by the /todo review rubric only.
Decision criterion: is the value worth the schema/validator churn,
or is review-time enforcement enough? Record the chosen path and
rationale in this TODO before w2 starts. Both paths still get the
rubric update in w3 -- that work is unconditional.
work_units.summary: Decide schema vs convention path for upstream-evidence TODOs; document decision

work_units.notes:
If schema path: add `freshness_check:` field, extend
`validate_todo.py`, document in `_project/TODO_ENTRY_TEMPLATE.yaml`.
If convention path: extend `_project/TODO_ENTRY_TEMPLATE.yaml` with
a worked `w0:` example and call out the naming convention in
`.claude/skills/todo/SKILL.md`.
work_units.summary: Implement the chosen freshness mechanism (schema field OR strong w0 convention)

work_units.notes:
Add a freshness axis to `.claude/skills/todo/SKILL.md` review
rubric that fires on TODOs whose `description` cites upstream
evidence (specific version, harness PASS, observed behavior). The
axis scores 0-3 on whether the TODO has a runnable re-validation
command and whether the resolved version is bound to the TODO.
This work runs regardless of w1's choice; the schema vs convention
decision affects implementation but the rubric still needs the
axis either way.
work_units.summary: Extend /todo review rubric with a freshness axis (unconditional)

work_units.notes:
Create `_project/verification-logs/README.md` documenting:
"commit captured stdout under
`_project/verification-logs/<todo-id>/<work-id>.log` for
verification-only work units." Add a `.gitkeep` so the path
exists even when empty. Update `.claude/skills/code/SKILL.md`
(debug/iterate notes) to point at the convention for evidence-
only commits.

Pick one current TODO whose work units include re-running an
external harness (e.g. a `track-upstream-platform-workarounds`
child item) and apply the new convention as a worked example.
Reference the example from the TODO_ENTRY_TEMPLATE comment so the
next author finds it immediately.
work_units.summary: Apply the convention to one in-flight TODO as a reference example

work_units.notes:
Recommended by blind-spot `2026-05-04-074634` (third item).
Grep `_project/TODO/*/planning/` for descriptions citing
"retire", "remove workaround", "narrow cap once upstream", or
"drop deprecation once Python X.Y" -- any 2+ matches confirm
that the schema/convention pays for itself. List matches in
this TODO's notes. If 0-1 matches, the work in w1-w5 still
ships but the schema-level option (vs convention) loses some
of its justification.
work_units.summary: Sweep planning/ for sibling 'retire workaround once upstream lands' TODOs
